quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: FULL-YEAR GUIDANCE PATH (CFO Stansbury). 'We're still committed to the guidance that we laid out, obviously we don't guide revenue, or at least we haven't to date.' The State of California delivery the plan had partly expected in the second half was accelerated into Q2 - 'that's now done'. On EBITDA: 'if you look historically, Adjusted EBITDA is about $100 million less than the third quarter than the second quarter, just seasonally because of summer maintenance and energy costs', and looking at what the fourth quarter 'would need to be to hit guidance, I think that solidifies what we're saying for the year.' Modernization and simplification savings, on track, are 'frankly a big piece of how we inflect EBITDA this year, while revenue hasn't inflected yet. The revenue decline slowing is certainly a help.' Alkira is not in the Investor Day targets; its impact on growth is being quantified and will be shared 'when we provide our 2027 guidance'. North America total business revenue was down 1.6% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 guidance maintained; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA historically about $100 million below Q2 (seasonal); North America total business -1.6% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: ALKIRA EARLY COMMERCIAL SIGNALS AND DIGITAL ECONOMICS. CEO Johnson, hedged ('it's been a month since we've closed, so I don't want to overdo our zeal here'): 'When we renew Alkira customers, we're upsizing the deals ... We have several data points that show that', and with Multi-Cloud Gateway and the Alkira portfolio Lumen is 'a couple clicks up from procurement, talking about total network upgrades strategically to allow for them to achieve their AI ambitions ... knocking on the door of the CIO and CTO' - a larger share of wallet is 'our aspiration'. She is 'confident that Alkira will accelerate our strategic revenue growth curve'. CFO Stansbury: Alkira revenue and cost 'are immaterial in terms of our results at this point. It obviously had no impact on the second quarter'; MRR per Alkira customer is 'too early to say'; once a second, third or fourth service is added on a port 'you get very close to having zero marginal cost, and little to no CapEx'; on digital revenue, the Investor Day mix laid out 'as a baseline, that's still a good way to look at it ... It will go up.'

CALL-ONLY: PUBLIC SECTOR AND FEDERAL (CFO Stansbury). The accelerated State of California milestone hit both PCF revenue and public sector revenue ('It's both'). 'The public sector business obviously has been, I would say, fairly chunky given what's going on in the world. We also know third quarter is the strongest quarter for that business.' And: 'we remain in deep conversations around some fairly strategic investments with the federal government, we'll see where that takes us.'

CALL-ONLY: SECURITY PARTNERSHIP WITH PALO ALTO NETWORKS (CEO Johnson): 'We just paired Black Lotus Labs network-level threat intelligence with Palo Alto Networks' leading security platform to create a managed offering that's better together', and Lumen is 'scaling this partner model in the connected ecosystem' - Lumen network intelligence and fiber combined with tech partners' products.

CALL-ONLY: VOICE EXIT AND COPPER (management). CEO Johnson: the enterprise voice wind-down is segmented by customer - a huge number of customers with very small MRR versus a smaller number with a very large book of business - and 'intersecting that with our strategy to exit copper'; the order is customer first, 'second thing is maximize cash from it, and the third thing is to exit so that we can mine the copper', with regulatory constraints in some places. For replacement, 'Whether it's fixed wireless or satellite, we have the capability to drop a Starlink puck in place of the infrastructure site that they have today ... we're starting to get that motion in place to do it at scale.' CFO Stansbury: end of sale is announced; 'End of life is a different story, we're going to be aggressive about that'.
